description: Hand-verified ground truth benchmark question set measuring agent accuracy across path existence, no-path negative cases, architectural exposure, deterministic ranking, and remediation guidance.

cases.title: Direct Dependency Path Verification
cases.question: Does authentication-service have a dependency path to vulnerable jsonwebtoken@8.5.1?

expected_answer.conclusion: Yes, a direct dependency path exists from authentication-service to jsonwebtoken@8.5.1 (depth 1).
expected_answer.explanation: Graph traversal reveals that authentication-service directly imports jsonwebtoken@8.5.1 as declared in its package manifest. Shortest hop distance is 1.
forbidden_claims: Claim that path does not exist
Claim that dependency is transitive (depth > 1)
required_caveats: Path represents architectural reachability, not proof of runtime exploitability.

verification.verification_notes: Verified with Cypher traversal get_project_finding_paths; single DIRECT edge confirmed.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Verified direct dependency in package.json manifest.

cases.title: Transitive Two-Hop Dependency Path
cases.question: What is the shortest reachability path from order-service to find-my-way@3.0.0?

expected_answer.conclusion: The shortest path is transitive with depth 2: order-service -> fastify@3.29.0 -> find-my-way@3.0.0.
expected_answer.explanation: order-service directly depends on the fastify HTTP framework, which in turn transitively imports the find-my-way router package.
forbidden_claims: Claim that find-my-way is a direct dependency
Claim that no path exists
required_caveats: Reachability demonstrates architectural exposure through package dependency chains.

verification.verification_notes: Verified transitive path in lockfile fixture via FalkorDB bounded shortest-path traversal.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Checked lockfile tree: order-service -> fastify -> find-my-way.

cases.title: Deep Multi-Hop Bounded Traversal
cases.question: How many hops separate checkout-service from vulnerable lodash@4.17.15, and what intermediate packages are traversed?

expected_answer.conclusion: Exactly 3 hops separate checkout-service from lodash@4.17.15 via auth-client@1.2.0 and token-verifier@2.1.0.
expected_answer.explanation: The shortest path traverses checkout-service -> auth-client@1.2.0 -> token-verifier@2.1.0 -> lodash@4.17.15, establishing a 3-hop transitive chain.
forbidden_claims: Hallucinating depth 1 or 2
Omitting token-verifier intermediate node
required_caveats: Absence of shorter paths is confirmed within bounded search depth 8.

verification.verification_notes: Verified depth 3 shortest-path using bounded Cypher traversal *1..8.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Checked 3-hop chain structure and verified bounded depth.

cases.title: Cross-Service RPC Call Chain to Vulnerable Dependency
cases.question: Does web-frontend reach vulnerable redis-parser@3.0.0 across service boundaries?

expected_answer.conclusion: Yes, web-frontend reaches redis-parser@3.0.0 across service boundaries via cart-service (web-frontend -[CALLS]-> cart-service -[DEPENDS_ON]-> redis-parser@3.0.0).
expected_answer.explanation: The reachability path spans both service architecture and package dependencies: web-frontend communicates with cart-service via synthetic RPC call edge, and cart-service depends on redis-parser@3.0.0.
required_evidence: Provenance: origin synthetic on service call
forbidden_claims: Claiming web-frontend directly imports redis-parser
Omitting the intermediate microservice
required_caveats: Service call edge provenance is synthetic; package dependency is manifest-backed.

verification.verification_notes: Verified heterogeneous path combining CALLS relationship and DEPENDS_ON relationship.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Confirmed heterogeneous edge traversal and provenance labels.

cases.title: Disjoint Microservice Architecture Boundary
cases.question: Can payment-processor reach vulnerable pyyaml@5.3.1?

expected_answer.conclusion: No dependency path found from payment-processor to pyyaml@5.3.1 within evaluated traversal bounds.
expected_answer.explanation: pyyaml@5.3.1 is utilized exclusively within the disjoint analytics worker stack. The payment-processor dependency graph shares no directed edges or service calls to pyyaml.
forbidden_claims: Claim that absence of path guarantees the application is completely secure
Claiming a path exists because pyyaml exists in project repository
required_caveats: No path found is bounded by analyzed depth; it does not guarantee absence of unanalyzed exposure.

verification.verification_notes: FalkorDB query returns 0 paths for payment-processor root node to pyyaml package version.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Checked that no-path honest warning is mandated.

cases.title: Unreferenced Package Version in Ecosystem Index
cases.question: Is vulnerable uritools@3.0.0 reached by notification-service in the active project graph?

expected_answer.conclusion: No path exists from notification-service to uritools@3.0.0; the package version exists in the ecosystem node catalog but has zero inbound dependency edges.
expected_answer.explanation: While uritools@3.0.0 is stored in the database from global advisory feeds, notification-service has no manifest or lockfile references linking to it.
forbidden_claims: Claiming that advisory ingestion implies active project reachability
required_caveats: Absence of dependency relationship indicates unreferenced package, not an exploitability guarantee.

verification.verification_notes: Verified package node has in-degree 0 from notification-service cluster.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Confirmed ecosystem catalog isolation from service dependencies.

cases.title: Development Dependency Isolation from Production Runtime
cases.question: Does devDependencies-only jest@26.6.3 expose the production api-service runtime?

expected_answer.conclusion: No, devDependencies are pruned from production container images and excluded from the production service dependency graph.
expected_answer.explanation: jest@26.6.3 is declared exclusively under devDependencies in package.json. Production manifests omit build-time and test frameworks, leaving no runtime dependency path.
required_evidence: Scope: devDependencies excluded from runtime graph
forbidden_claims: Claiming that devDependencies expose the production runtime service
Conflating dev toolchain with production attack surface
Claiming that absence of path guarantees project is completely safe
required_caveats: Conclusion applies to production runtime container manifests; absence of runtime path does not guarantee safety.

verification.verification_notes: Verified runtime manifest graph prunes devDependencies; 0 paths returned.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Verified devDependencies pruning policy.

cases.title: Unidirectional Background Worker Boundary
cases.question: Can background batch-exporter trigger or reach vulnerable express@4.16.0 HTTP routes?

expected_answer.conclusion: No path found; batch-exporter is an offline producer with no inbound listeners or dependency edges to express@4.16.0.
expected_answer.explanation: batch-exporter only publishes messages to object storage and message brokers. express@4.16.0 is deployed in web-facing APIs, with no directed path connecting batch-exporter to express.
forbidden_claims: Claiming bidirectional reachability between independent microservices
Claiming that absence of path guarantees project is completely safe
required_caveats: No path found indicates absence of directed traversal edge within bounded depth 8; does not guarantee absolute safety.

verification.verification_notes: Traversed graph from batch-exporter service node; confirmed 0 directed paths to express.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Confirmed unidirectional topology edge enforcement.

cases.title: Public Ingress Entrypoint Exposure
cases.question: Is vulnerable node-forge@0.10.0 architecturally exposed to internet ingress?

expected_answer.conclusion: Yes, public-api has internet_facing=true and reaches node-forge@0.10.0 at depth 2 (public-api -> crypto-utils -> node-forge@0.10.0).
expected_answer.explanation: The service node public-api declares internet_facing=true, meaning inbound network requests from the public internet reach crypto-utils which depends on vulnerable node-forge.
forbidden_claims: Claiming that finding is actively exploitable or weaponized in production
required_caveats: Architectural exposure establishes structural reachability, not proof of runtime exploitability.

verification.verification_notes: Verified internet_facing property is true on public-api service node, and 2-hop path exists.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Strictly checked non-exploitability wording.

cases.title: Internal-Only Worker Service Exposure Boundary
cases.question: What is the network exposure boundary for xml2js@0.4.23 reached by offline-batch-job?

expected_answer.conclusion: Internal only; offline-batch-job has internet_facing=false and has no public ingress routes.
expected_answer.explanation: While xml2js@0.4.23 is directly reachable from offline-batch-job (depth 1), the service is strictly internal with internet_facing=false.
forbidden_claims: Claiming public internet exposure
Claiming service is safe from internal exposure
Claiming finding is exploitable or weaponized in production
required_caveats: Absence of public ingress reduces exposure boundary to internal cluster networks; reachability does not prove exploitability.

verification.verification_notes: Verified internet_facing property is false on offline-batch-job.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Confirmed internal boundary and reachability synthesis.

cases.title: Missing Ingress Metadata Handling
cases.question: How does Vulnify evaluate the exposure of legacy-importer when its internet-facing ingress signal is missing?

expected_answer.conclusion: Exposure is evaluated as unknown; Vulnify preserves uncertainty and never defaults missing ingress metadata to safe or zero risk.
expected_answer.explanation: When a service manifest does not specify internet_facing (value is null), Vulnify marks network exposure as unknown rather than assuming the service is internal.
required_evidence: Honesty rule: missing signal never defaulted to zero risk
forbidden_claims: Defaulting missing signal to internet_facing=false
Assuming legacy-importer is safe
Claiming unconfirmed exploitability without evidence
required_caveats: Unknown ingress metadata requires manual operator verification; exposure is unconfirmed, not proven exploitable.

verification.verification_notes: Verified scoring policy section 1.1 tenet 2: missing signals explicitly treated as unknown.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Verified adherence to missing signal tenets.

cases.title: Edge Provenance Distinction (Manifest vs Synthetic)
cases.question: Are synthetic edges present in the reachability path from gateway-service to bcryptjs@2.4.3?

expected_answer.conclusion: Yes, the path combines a synthetic RPC call edge (origin: synthetic) to auth-service and a manifest lockfile edge (origin: manifest) to bcryptjs@2.4.3.
expected_answer.explanation: Vulnify records edge provenance explicitly. The gateway-service -> auth-service edge was inferred synthetically from network configuration, while the auth-service -> bcryptjs edge was parsed from package-lock.json, documenting heterogeneous architectural exposure.
forbidden_claims: Claiming all edges are manifest-verified
Claiming synthetic edges are real production traces
Claiming finding is runtime exploitable
required_caveats: Synthetic edges represent inferred architectural connections subject to runtime verification; reachability demonstrates exposure but does not prove exploitability.

verification.verification_notes: Verified edge property origin on each relationship in traversal result.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Checked provenance property validation on graph edges.

cases.title: Highest Priority Band Assignment and Reasons
cases.question: Why is finding find-crit-001 (OSV-EXAMPLE-CRIT-001) assigned to the Highest priority band?

expected_answer.conclusion: find-crit-001 is placed in the Highest priority band because it has severity CRITICAL, version match affected, and a confirmed reachable path (depth 1).
expected_answer.explanation: Under Vulnify scoring policy v1.0.0, Critical severity combined with confirmed reachability from an active service triggers the Highest priority band.
forbidden_claims: Assigning High or Medium band
Claiming exploitability was proven
required_caveats: Policy v1.0.0 priority reflects architectural exposure and severity, not CVSS alone.

verification.verification_notes: Verified with Vulnify Scoring Engine v1.0.0 execution: band Highest assigned.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Verified scoring engine output against docs/scoring.md.

cases.title: High Severity Finding with No Path Downgrade
cases.question: What priority band is assigned to a High-severity finding when graph traversal returns no path found?

expected_answer.conclusion: It is assigned to the Medium priority band; high-severity findings with unconfirmed reachability are downgraded to Medium, never dropped to Low.
expected_answer.explanation: According to scoring policy v1.0.0 Band 3 rule 2, severity HIGH with path_status no_path_found falls back to Medium priority to account for potential unanalyzed exposure.
required_evidence: Downgrade rule: HIGH severity + no_path_found -> Medium
forbidden_claims: Assigning Low priority
Assigning High priority despite no path
required_caveats: No path found does not guarantee safety; Medium band preserves cautious attention.

verification.verification_notes: Verified scoring engine Band 3 rule 2: HIGH severity + no path = Medium band.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Checked fallback rule in scoring.md.

cases.title: Unknown Severity Signal Prioritization
cases.question: How does the scoring engine prioritize a finding when upstream advisory severity is unknown?

expected_answer.conclusion: It is assigned to the Medium priority band; missing severity is treated as UNKNOWN and handled conservatively, never assumed to be Low or zero risk.
expected_answer.explanation: Scoring policy v1.0.0 Band 3 rule 4 places findings with confirmed paths and UNKNOWN severity into Medium priority, citing SEVERITY_UNKNOWN.
forbidden_claims: Defaulting unknown severity to LOW
Placing finding in Low priority band
required_caveats: Missing upstream signal is treated with caution, not zero risk.

verification.verification_notes: Verified scoring engine Band 3 rule 4: path_found + severity UNKNOWN = Medium.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Confirmed missing signal policy.

cases.title: Deterministic Tie-Breaking Between Identical Priority Findings
cases.question: How does Vulnify break ties between two High-priority findings with identical HIGH severity?

expected_answer.conclusion: Vulnify evaluates deterministic Tie-Breakers in order: Tie-Breaker 3 (path presence), Tie-Breaker 4 (path depth ascending: shorter path first), Tie-Breaker 5 (actionable fix availability), and Tie-Breaker 6 (alphanumeric sort).
expected_answer.explanation: When band weight and severity rank are tied, Tie-Breaker 4 prioritizes direct dependencies (depth 1) over transitive ones (depth > 1). If depths match, findings with published fixed versions rank higher.
forbidden_claims: Claiming ties are broken randomly
Relying on nondeterministic database row order
required_caveats: Tie-breaking order is completely deterministic and documented in scoring.md section 4.

verification.verification_notes: Verified sorting key implementation in vulnify.scoring.engine.rank_project_findings.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Checked sorting tuple matches docs/scoring.md tie-breaker order.

cases.title: Actionable Upstream Patch Upgrade Recommendation
cases.question: What is the recommended non-breaking upgrade for semver@5.7.1 affected by OSV-EXAMPLE-PATCH-001?

expected_answer.conclusion: Upgrade to semver@5.7.2; this is an actionable patch-level fix with low breaking risk, though project regression testing is recommended.
expected_answer.explanation: Upstream advisory OSV-EXAMPLE-PATCH-001 lists 5.7.2 in fixed_versions. Upgrading from 5.7.1 to 5.7.2 is a patch jump preserving API compatibility.
forbidden_claims: Recommending major upgrade 6.0.0 when patch 5.7.2 exists
Claiming upgrade is 100% safe without testing
required_caveats: Absence of detected conflicts does not guarantee runtime compatibility; integration testing is required.

verification.verification_notes: Verified fixed_versions contains 5.7.2 and semver diff is patch.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Confirmed SemVer jump calculation and safety caveat.

cases.title: Remediation Guidance When No Upstream Fix Exists
cases.question: What remediation recommendation is provided for unmaintained-parser@1.0.0 when OSV-EXAMPLE-NOFIX-001 has no fixed version?

expected_answer.conclusion: The system reports that no fixed version is available upstream; it advises alternative defensive measures (package substitution or network isolation) and never invents a fictional patch version.
expected_answer.explanation: When advisory fixed_versions is empty, Vulnify explicitly states that no remediation target exists upstream, advising architectural defense-in-depth instead of hallucinating a release.
required_evidence: Status: No known fixed version published
forbidden_claims: Inventing a nonexistent 2.0.0 or 1.0.1 release
Claiming the issue is unresolvable without defensive guidance
required_caveats: Remediation target unknown requires security team architectural review.

verification.verification_notes: Verified advisory record has empty fixed_versions list; guidance follows honesty policy.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Strictly verified absence of hallucinated patch versions.

cases.title: Major SemVer Jump Compatibility Assessment
cases.question: How does Vulnify classify the SemVer compatibility risk of upgrading axios from 0.21.1 to 1.6.0?

expected_answer.conclusion: It is classified as a Major SemVer Jump (0.x to 1.x) with high probability of breaking API changes, requiring thorough integration and regression testing.
expected_answer.explanation: Transitioning from 0.21.1 to 1.6.0 crosses a major version boundary. Under Semantic Versioning conventions, major increments signal potentially breaking API modifications.
forbidden_claims: Claiming the upgrade is non-breaking
Classifying 0.x to 1.x as a patch jump
required_caveats: Breaking changes require code review and API regression testing before deployment.

verification.verification_notes: Verified semver parser categorizes 0.21.1 -> 1.6.0 as major jump.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Confirmed major version classification.

cases.title: GitHub Issue Remediation Approval Gating and Data Integrity
cases.question: What security controls prevent the agent from automatically creating a GitHub remediation issue or submitting hostile advisory HTML?

expected_answer.conclusion: Issue creation is write-gated, requiring explicit human approval (confirmed: true) bound to a SHA-256 plan hash; untrusted advisory text is neutralized into quoted Markdown blocks and never rendered as HTML.
expected_answer.explanation: Under US-504, open_fix_issue fails closed if confirmed is false. The plan hash ensures the created issue matches the approved preview. Under US-604, HTML entities are escaped and external text is isolated in blockquotes.
forbidden_claims: Claiming the agent can create issues autonomously without human approval
Claiming raw HTML is executed or rendered
required_caveats: Agent is unauthorized to execute state-mutating actions without operator confirmation.

verification.verification_notes: Verified open_fix_issue tool definition has requires_approval=True and validates plan_hash.

reviews.notes: Verified against FalkorDB Cypher path queries and graph schema conventions.
Verified write gating and US-604 HTML neutralization.
